title: New Heart Disease Drugs Fail to Show Expected Benefits
subtitle: Recent medical studies reveal that two promising treatments did not prevent heart attacks or strokes in high-risk patients.

summary.en: Researchers recently tested two new drugs designed to prevent heart disease. Despite high hopes, both medications failed to reduce the number of heart attacks or strokes in patients. One drug targeted inflammation, while the other focused on a specific protein in the blood. Experts are now working to understand why these treatments did not work as expected. The findings highlight the complexity of treating advanced heart disease.
summary.zh: 研究人員近期測試了兩款旨在預防心臟病的新藥。儘管寄予厚望，這兩款藥物皆未能減少患者心臟病發作或中風的次數。其中一款藥物針對發炎反應，另一款則鎖定血液中的特定蛋白質。專家們目前正致力於釐清為何這些治療方式未達預期效果。這些發現凸顯了治療晚期心臟病的複雜性。

paragraphs.en: Medical researchers recently shared disappointing news regarding two new drugs that were expected to help prevent heart disease. Doctors had high hopes that these treatments would protect patients from heart attacks and strokes, but large studies showed that neither drug provided the expected benefits. These results were presented at the American Heart Association annual meeting in Chicago and published in the New England Journal of Medicine.
paragraphs.zh: 醫學研究人員近期分享了關於兩款新藥令人失望的消息，這兩款藥物原先被寄予厚望，能協助預防心臟病。醫師們曾高度期待這些治療方式能保護患者免於心臟病發作與中風，但大型研究顯示，這兩款藥物皆未達到預期的效益。這些研究結果已在芝加哥舉行的美國心臟協會（American Heart Association）年會上發表，並刊登於《新英格蘭醫學期刊》（New England Journal of Medicine）。

paragraphs.en: The first study looked at a drug called ziltivekimab. This medicine was designed to lower inflammation, which is the body's response to injury or infection. According to MedPage Today, researchers found that while the drug successfully lowered inflammatory markers in the blood, it did not reduce the number of heart attacks, strokes, or deaths in patients. Paul M. Ridker, a doctor at Harvard Medical School, noted that the patients in this study had advanced heart disease and kidney problems. He suggested that for these patients, the disease might have already reached a stage where anti-inflammatory drugs are no longer effective.
paragraphs.zh: 第一項研究針對一款名為 ziltivekimab 的藥物進行測試。該藥物旨在降低發炎反應，即人體對受傷或感染所產生的反應。根據《今日醫學新聞》（MedPage Today）報導，研究人員發現，儘管該藥物成功降低了血液中的發炎指標，卻未能減少患者心臟病發作、中風或死亡的案例。哈佛醫學院（Harvard Medical School）醫師瑞德克（Paul M. Ridker）指出，參與此項研究的患者多患有晚期心臟病與腎臟問題。他認為對於這些患者而言，疾病可能已發展至抗發炎藥物不再有效的階段。

paragraphs.en: A second study focused on a different approach. Doctors tested a drug called pelacarsen, which was designed to lower levels of a protein in the blood called lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a). High levels of this protein have long been linked to a higher risk of heart disease. According to NPR, about one billion people worldwide have high levels of this protein. Steven Nissen, a cardiologist at the Cleveland Clinic who led the study, stated that he was shocked by the results. Although the drug successfully lowered Lp(a) levels by about 78 percent, patients who took the medicine did not have fewer heart attacks or strokes compared to those who took a placebo—a pill with no medicine in it used for comparison.
paragraphs.zh: 第二項研究則採取了不同的途徑。醫師們測試了一款名為 pelacarsen 的藥物，其設計目的是降低血液中一種稱為脂蛋白（a）〔lipoprotein(a)，簡稱 Lp(a)〕的蛋白質濃度。長期以來，這種蛋白質濃度過高一直被認為與較高的心臟病風險有關。根據美國公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，全球約有十億人體內含有高濃度的此類蛋白質。主持該研究的克里夫蘭診所（Cleveland Clinic）心臟科醫師尼森（Steven Nissen）表示，他對結果感到震驚。儘管該藥物成功將 Lp(a) 濃度降低了約 78%，但服用該藥物的患者與服用安慰劑（即不含藥物成分、僅供對照用的藥丸）的患者相比，心臟病發作或中風的次數並未減少。

paragraphs.en: These results were unexpected because many experts believed these drugs would be major breakthroughs. Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in many developed countries, and doctors are constantly searching for new ways to help patients who already follow healthy habits. Many of these patients eat well, exercise, and keep their cholesterol and blood pressure under control, yet they still suffer from heart problems. Harlan Krumholz, a cardiologist at Yale University, described the failure of the pelacarsen study as "jarring" because the expectations for success were so high.
paragraphs.zh: 這些結果出乎意料，因為許多專家原先認為這些藥物將是重大的突破。心血管疾病在許多已開發國家仍是頭號死因，醫師們也不斷尋求新方法來協助那些已經維持健康習慣的患者。這些患者中，許多人飲食均衡、規律運動，並將膽固醇與血壓控制在理想範圍內，卻仍飽受心臟問題之苦。耶魯大學（Yale University）心臟科醫師克魯姆霍茲（Harlan Krumholz）形容 pelacarsen 研究的失敗令人「感到震驚」，因為各界對其成功的期待實在太高了。

paragraphs.en: So, what went wrong? Researchers are currently trying to understand these results. Regarding the inflammation drug, Dr. Ridker explained that while genetic data suggested that the pathway being targeted was important, there is a difference between genetic influence and the ability to reverse a disease once it has started. He noted that the body's inflammatory systems are "exceptionally complex." For the Lp(a) study, some scientists are now questioning if high levels of this protein actually cause heart disease, or if it is simply a marker that appears when other problems are already present.
paragraphs.zh: 那麼，究竟哪裡出了問題？研究人員目前正試圖釐清這些結果。關於發炎藥物，瑞德克醫師解釋道，雖然基因數據顯示該藥物鎖定的路徑很重要，但基因影響與逆轉已發生的疾病之間仍存在差異。他指出，人體的發炎系統「極其複雜」。至於 Lp(a) 的研究，部分科學家現在開始質疑，高濃度的這種蛋白質究竟是否為導致心臟病的元兇，還是僅僅是一種在其他問題出現時才會顯現的指標。

paragraphs.en: Despite these setbacks, experts remain committed to finding new solutions. Novartis, the company that made pelacarsen, stated that the study provides important information that will help guide future research. Meanwhile, Dr. Ridker noted that other studies on ziltivekimab are still ongoing for different groups of patients, and he remains optimistic about those trials. He also reminded patients that there are still effective ways to manage heart health. Clinicians can help patients reduce inflammation and risk through lifestyle changes, such as healthy eating, regular exercise, and stopping smoking. Additionally, existing medications like statins—drugs that lower cholesterol—have already been proven to improve outcomes for many people.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管遭遇這些挫折，專家們仍致力於尋找新的解決方案。製造 pelacarsen 的諾華公司（Novartis）表示，該研究提供了重要的資訊，將有助於引導未來的研究方向。與此同時，瑞德克醫師提到，針對不同患者群體的 ziltivekimab 其他研究仍在進行中，他對這些試驗仍保持樂觀。他也提醒患者，目前仍有有效的方法可以管理心臟健康。臨床醫師可以透過生活型態的改變，例如健康飲食、規律運動與戒菸，協助患者降低發炎反應與風險。此外，現有的藥物如史他汀類藥物（statins，即降低膽固醇的藥物），已被證實能改善許多人的健康預後。

paragraphs.en: These findings serve as a reminder that medical science is a difficult process. Even when a treatment works exactly as intended in the laboratory, it may not always lead to better health outcomes in the real world. As researchers continue to study these complex diseases, they will use these results to refine their approach and look for new, more effective ways to protect patients in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 這些發現提醒我們，醫學科學是一項艱難的過程。即使治療方式在實驗室中完全符合預期，也不見得總能在現實世界中帶來更好的健康結果。隨著研究人員持續深入研究這些複雜的疾病，他們將利用這些結果來精進研究方法，並在未來尋求更有效的方式來保護患者。

quiz.question: According to the study on pelacarsen, what was the specific outcome regarding the drug's effect on the body?

options.A: It failed to lower the levels of lipoprotein(a) in the patients' blood.
options.B: It successfully reduced the target protein levels but did not decrease the incidence of heart attacks.
options.C: It caused more heart attacks and strokes compared to the group taking the placebo.
options.D: It proved that high levels of lipoprotein(a) are not related to heart disease at all.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，研究顯示 pelacarsen 成功將 Lp(a) 蛋白質水平降低了約 78%，但服用該藥物的患者在心臟病發作或中風的發生率上，與服用安慰劑的對照組相比並無減少。選項 A 錯誤，因為藥物確實降低了蛋白質；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到藥物導致更多病發；選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到科學家現在質疑該蛋白質是否為致病原因，而非完全否定其與心臟病的關聯。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the patients who participated in the ziltivekimab study?

options.A: They were generally healthy individuals who wanted to prevent future heart problems.
options.B: They had previously failed to respond to cholesterol-lowering medications like statins.
options.C: They likely had significant, long-standing health issues before starting the drug trial.
options.D: They were primarily young people who had just been diagnosed with early-stage heart disease.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第二段，Paul M. Ridker 醫生指出，參與 ziltivekimab 研究的患者患有「晚期心臟病」及「腎臟問題」。這暗示這些患者在試驗開始前，身體狀況已經相當複雜且嚴重。選項 A 錯誤，因為他們並非健康人；選項 B 文中未提及；選項 D 錯誤，文中明確指出是晚期（advanced）而非早期（early-stage）心臟病。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'jarring' mean as used by Harlan Krumholz?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文章第四段中，Harlan Krumholz 描述研究失敗的結果為「jarring」，意指因為原先對藥物成功的期望很高，結果卻不如預期，這種巨大的落差感令人感到震驚且不快。選項 B 錯誤，此處並非指物理上的噪音；選項 C 雖然研究結果令人困惑，但「jarring」強調的是情緒上的衝擊而非技術上的複雜度；選項 D 錯誤，該詞與緩慢無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the two new heart disease drugs?

options.A: The pharmaceutical industry is intentionally hiding the truth about ineffective heart medications.
options.B: Medical research is an unpredictable process where laboratory success does not guarantee real-world clinical benefits.
options.C: Doctors should stop prescribing existing treatments like statins because they are no longer considered effective.
options.D: Inflammation and protein levels are completely irrelevant to the study of cardiovascular disease.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章最後一段總結了全文的核心觀點：醫學研究是一項困難的過程，即便藥物在實驗室中運作良好，也不一定能轉化為現實世界中的健康改善。選項 A 過度推論，文中並無提到隱瞞真相；選項 C 與文章第六段內容矛盾，文中提到 statins 仍被證實有效；選項 D 錯誤，文章僅是探討這些指標與治療效果之間的複雜關係，並未否定其重要性。
